32.text: Some single-piece pipes are ornamented with patterns inlaid with pewter

33.text: (Fig. 119, b, c). The bowl and the mouth-piece are of pewter, and are cast

34.text: in wooden mantles (Fig. 120). The wooden part of the pipe, with its sur-

35.text: face grooved for inlaying, is interposed between the end moulds, which are

36.text: connected by a paper tube. The metal parts are thus all cast at the same

37.text: time, the pewter being poured into the bowl-end of the mould. The pipe is

38.text: afterwards finished with a knife and a file.

40.text: of wood. Its shape is nearer to that usual among Europeans, and may be

41.text: an imitation. The bowl is adorned with very clever carvings. This work is
